final_task_tree.title: Figure out a training plan for my dog
final_task_tree.description:
Rescue border collie mix, 14 months. Pulls hard on the leash and barks at every other dog on walks. South Bay, California; I can do evenings and weekends.

Three things only:
1. Whether to hire a trainer or do it myself.
2. If hiring — two or three local options with real prices.
3. A week-by-week plan for the first four weeks.

Don't research anything beyond those three.

subtasks.title: Decide: DIY vs. hire a trainer for leash pulling + dog reactivity
subtasks.description: Work out whether a 14-month rescue border collie mix with hard leash pulling and barking/lunging at other dogs is a DIY case or needs a professional. Key question: is this reactivity (fear/frustration) or just under-exercised adolescent excitement, and what does that imply. Output: a clear recommendation with reasoning and cost/time trade-off.

subtasks.title: Find 3 South Bay trainers with real published prices
subtasks.description:
THREE OPTIONS, cheapest to most expensive. All use reward-based / positive-reinforcement methods.

1) HUMANE SOCIETY SILICON VALLEY — "Top Dogs Level 1" — $300
- Built specifically for leash/barrier reactivity. Six-week course; first session 90 min, then 5 x 50 min. For dogs who bark, lunge, or worry but have NOT caused injury. Dogs under 8 months need instructor approval (yours is 14 mo, fine).
- Next listed start: Aug 19, 2026, 6:15pm, online-only via Zoom (6 weeks). In-person Top Dogs 1/2/3 also run — Level 2 is in-person and requires Level 1 or instructor approval.
- Adopters get a discount code — email DogTraining@hssv.org and ask, since your dog is a rescue (ask whether an HSSV adoption is required).
- HSSV does NOT offer private training/consults to the public, but will give referrals.
- 901 Ames Ave, Milpitas, CA 95035. Email DogTraining@hssv.org
- Pages: https://www.hssv.org/behavior-management-classes/ and https://www.hssv.org/services/dog-services/training/
- Free resource regardless of whether you enroll: HSSV Reactive Dog Training Guide PDF — https://www.hssv.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Reactive-Dog-Training-Guide-7.11.25.pdf

2) STACY'S WAG'N'TRAIN (Stacy Braslau-Schneck, San Jose, 25+ yrs, in-home/virtual)
- Basic "4-pack": $800 — four 1-hour private lessons (starts with a virtual evaluation + 3 coaching sessions, virtual or in person), scheduled 1–2 weeks apart. Described as for basic training WITHOUT real behavior-mod needs — probably not enough on its own for reactivity.
- Beginning Behavior Modification "6-pack": $1,500 — six 1-hour private lessons (virtual eval + 5 coaching). This is the right tier for leash reactivity.
- Behavior Modification Foundation: $3,000 — 14 one-hour lessons.
- Contact: stacy@wagntrain.com (email is the preferred/only listed channel). Serves Willow Glen and surrounding San Jose.
- https://wagntrain.com/private-dog-training-lessons/

3) D FOR DOGZ (Kaajal; Silicon Valley — covers San Jose, Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Mountain View, Campbell, Los Gatos, Cupertino, Milpitas)
- Has a dedicated leash-reactive private program; framing is emotion-first (counter-conditioning / learning to disengage), not suppression.
- Private Coaching: $2,400 / 6 weeks — you learn to train the dog; 90-minute sessions, between-session support by call/text/email, one complimentary group class, 3 months post-program phone/email support.
- Day Training: $4,200 / 6 weeks — trainer works the dog directly, you join key sessions. ($420 discount for enrolling in the full program.)
- Phone: 650-538-3011. https://dfordogtraining.com/private-dog-training-silicon-valley/leash-reactive-dog-private-training/

RULED OUT: Off Leash K9 / Sit Means Sit / Bark Busters — e-collar / dominance-based approaches. With a reactive dog, punishing the bark tends to suppress the warning while leaving the underlying fear/frustration, and can make reactivity worse. Skip these.

subtasks.title: Write the week-by-week plan for weeks 1-4
subtasks.description: Build a concrete 4-week plan covering equipment, loose-leash walking protocol, and a dog-reactivity protocol (engage-disengage / look-at-that / counter-conditioning at distance). Must fit evenings and weekends. Include session lengths and what success looks like at the end of each week.

subtasks.title: Buy the equipment: front-clip harness + 6ft leash + high-value treats
subtasks.description: Front-clip (front-attachment) harness in the dog's size, a fixed 4-6ft leash (NOT retractable), a treat pouch, and soft high-value treats you can deliver fast (small cheese cubes, hot dog slices, freeze-dried liver). Optional: 15-30ft long line for the yard/park decompression work. Available at any Petco/PetSmart in the South Bay or online.

subtasks.title: Email or call your top 2 trainer picks to book an intake
subtasks.description: Contact details go in the trainer research subtask. Ask each: (1) do you use food-based/force-free methods and no prong/e-collar, (2) do you have evening or weekend slots, (3) what does the first session cost and what's included, (4) have you worked with adolescent herding-breed leash reactivity. Book whichever answers best.
